correctness.rationale: The two Kalman information recurrences have strictly positive denominators for p,q,r,s>0 and t>=0. Their exact difference factors into (r-s)(t/((t+nu C)(t+nu D))-1). Exact AM–GM minimization of the inverse ratio establishes the critical noise threshold; a convex quadratic gives all strict/tie cases. Factorization of the discriminant gives the square-root closing width; Vieta gives small-noise endpoint laws. An independent exact-rational checker passed 10016 assertions, including the full three-regime witness. The universal classification rests on the symbolic proof, not finite trials.

value.rationale: The source's budgeted finite-horizon sensor problem naturally includes two sensors available once. The result exactly classifies both feasible permutations for every positive prior, process noise and pair of precisions, detecting an unexpected strong-last/strong-first/strong-last reentrance with varying dynamics gain. A sharp noise threshold, explicit switching roots and the square-root disappearance of the favorable window quantify a design-sensitive boundary that generic mixed-integer optimization does not describe analytically. It is a natural complete classification with potential use in scheduling short-lived measurements, not a random parameter slice or isolated numerical counterexample.
